reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure, and let F be any normed additive commutative group. Let W : E → ℝ be continuous, and suppose that x ↦ exp(-W(x)) is integrable with respect to volume on E. Write μ for the tilted volume measure with potential -W, that is, volume weighted by exp(-W) and normalized. For every equivalence class a in L²(μ; F), let f : E → F be the representative selected by the displayed coercions from a. Then x ↦ ‖f(x)‖² is locally integrable with respect to volume on E: at every point it is integrable on some neighborhood. Moreover, for every compact set K ⊆ E, f belongs to MemLp with exponent 2 for volume restricted to K; in particular, f is almost-everywhere strongly measurable for that restricted measure and has finite squared-norm integral there. No global unweighted L² integrability of f is asserted.
objects: E and F; a potential W; volume on E; μ = volume.tilted (fun x => -W x); an Lp equivalence class a; its coercion-selected representative f; arbitrary compact subsets K of E.
domains: E : Type u_1 is a normed additive commutative group with an inner-product-space structure over ℝ, finite-dimensional over ℝ, and a measurable-space structure satisfying BorelSpace. F : Type u_2 is a normed additive commutative group. W : E → ℝ. a : Lp F 2 μ. f : E → F. K : Set E.
quantifiers: Universally quantify E and all displayed structures, F and its normed additive commutative group structure, and W. Assuming continuity of W and integrability of exp(-W), universally quantify a. For each a the two conclusions hold jointly, with the second universally quantifying K subject to IsCompact K.
assumptions: Exactly the displayed structures on E and F, Continuous W, and volume-integrability of x ↦ exp(-W(x)). Membership of a in the weighted Lp space is imposed through its quantified type. No linear, inner-product, finite-dimensional, or completeness assumption on F is present; no smoothness or convexity assumption on W is present.
conclusion: The squared norm of the selected representative is locally volume-integrable, and that same representative is MemLp at exponent 2 for volume restricted to every compact K.
scopes: The input a is an almost-everywhere equivalence class for the tilted measure; the conclusions concern its displayed coercion-selected function, not a separately quantified arbitrary representative. The local-integrability neighborhood can depend on the point and the given data. The compact-set conclusion holds for every compact K. Neither conclusion asserts global square-integrability with respect to unweighted volume.
constant_dependencies: There are no explicit constants, estimates, or quantitative bounds in the statement. Neighborhoods implicit in local integrability need not be uniform and can depend on the point, a, W, and the ambient structures.
